justification: Abstract's contribution is a pipeline that re-examines each cited frame before it is shown, i.e. a check that gates output; three verifier designs are ablated in a lab, no deployed use.

Contribution is the institutional arrangement itself, three isolated planner/executor/verifier agents with asymmetric contextual isolation, formalised as an architecture with only theoretical analysis and no experiment.
Abstract frames self-verification as a compute-control policy with adaptive stopping and fewer turns; trained and tested on seven math benchmarks in the lab, never deployed.
The novelty is planner-defined passing criteria encoded as subtask verification functions that gate handoffs; evaluated only on datasets against single- and multi-agent baselines.
Headline artefact is a taxonomy of completion-fabrication patterns plus a failure timeline, drawn from nine months of the author's own production use of a coding agent.

Contribution is how the verification is produced: a tool-flow interface that decouples verification modelling from exact execution for candidate-answer adjudication; tested on five math datasets in the lab.

Stated contribution is a verification methodology and drift decomposition for agent development, an instrument for measuring loop behaviour; evidence is ablation cells on ARC-AGI-3 with task efficacy null.
The novelty is planner-defined passing criteria encoded as subtask verification functions that gate handoffs; evaluated only on datasets against single- and multi-agent baselines.
Toolkit intervenes after an action is formulated but before execution to verify safety, a pre-execution gate; harm reduction measured across agentic tasks in the lab, not in a deployed setting.

Contribution is a diagnostic decomposition of the iterative pipeline into Generation/Verification/Reflection/Recalibration used to locate error sources across methods; run on HotpotQA, ALFWorld and HumanEval in the lab.
The novelty is how the judgement is produced: MCTS-driven multi-perspective LLM-as-a-judge with a unit-test-level reward for code correctness; validated on three benchmarks and five LLMs.

The claim is an enhanced reference-less LLM-as-a-judge validation metric checked against execution-based ground truth; refinement agents are downstream. Lab evaluation only, no live incident remediation studied.
Empirical audit of one named mechanism, LLM-as-a-judge scoring that gates refinement, showing prior scores anchor it; three prompt conditions deliberately varied over 192,000 evaluations.
Headline artefact is a benchmark of 20 processes plus an evaluation approach used to measure 16 LLMs and their self-improvement techniques; a lab assessment, no deployed BPM setting.
Contribution is the feedback learning loop in which a trained critic's real-time feedback is fed back to iteratively rewrite QA responses; measured as citation and MAUVE gains on datasets in the lab.

Contribution is the actor-critic revision step, a critic trained to emit fine-grained natural-language critiques and actionable revisions the actor applies; validated in three interactive environments.
Contribution is adaptive plan generation and in-plan/out-of-plan replanning that determines the agent's next step from environmental feedback; validated on ALFWorld and MiniWoB++ against baselines.
Contribution is a critique generator trained with RL so a frozen model can repair its outputs, i.e. the revise-on-feedback step; validated on three datasets against other critique generators.
Contribution is the arrangement of two agents and what they exchange, the recommender-user agent feedback loop prior work treated individually; validated on three datasets with 11-21% gains.

Contribution is error-driven self-correction: a mined error hierarchy trains an error-critic whose fine-grained feedback customises executor solution flows; validated on seven RAG datasets in the lab.
Contribution is how the step-level judgement is produced, a generative PRM doing CoT plus code verification before judging each step; validated on ProcessBench and math benchmarks.
Contribution is critic-guided sub-goal selection that decides the next reasoning or retrieval step; validated on competitive programming, theorem-driven math and domain retrieval against baselines.
The ablation credits the critic-based feedback loop, validator critiques guiding regeneration, rather than the multi-agent heterogeneity or model size; evidence is GSM8K accuracy gains in the lab.
Contribution is an outer data-flywheel loop in which the critic's own collected positive/negative samples train a stronger second-round critic; validated on several GUI datasets, not deployed.
Contribution is the Estimate-Verify-Update check that matches predicted outcomes against observations before beliefs are updated; validated across three embodied benchmarks plus a probing analysis.
